This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 16.09.2023 at about 06.30 a.m, the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-40-EG-6559 which was ridden by its rider, near K a m m a g a n a h a l l i V i l l a g e , C h i k k a b a l l a p u r a T a l u k , a t ( S C C H - 3 ) 3 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 that time all of a sudden
a Bharath Benz Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-43-A-2678 which was driven by its driver at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle.
Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to General hospital, Chikkaballapura,
wherein after first aid he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 16.09.2023 to 16.10.2023 and has undergone surgery.
The petitioner has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.

Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 20 years and was a student studying in 5th Sem. B.Com and also taking tution and was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he is unable to walk, sit, squat, claim stairs or do any work as he was doing prior to the accident and father and mother of the petitioner was earning Rs.500/- per day working as daily labour and both are suffered lot from his accident in the family.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending Tipper Lorry involved in the accident and in this regard the Peresandra Police have registered a case against (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 rider of the said offending Tipper Lorry.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- with interest and costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent, hence placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent is the insurer of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-43-A-2678 and the liability of this respondent, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act.

It is further denied age, avocation, income and education of the petitioner, manner of accident and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the petitioner was riding Motor Cycle on the road in a zig-zag speedy manner and on center of the road and dashed against the Tipper Lorry bearing Balaji Alias Balaji V vs Manjunatha Enterprises on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69890741/
2 No.KA-43-A-2678 and due to his negligent act the accident took place and the compensation claimed (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 is highly excessive and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01. Whether the petitioner is proves that he was sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 16.09.2023 at about 06.30 a.m, on Kammanahalli Village,
Chikkaballapura Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of Bharat Benz Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA-43-A-2678 by its driver as alleged in the petition ?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03
. What Order or Award?

06. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed disability as PW.2 and through them got marked 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24 and closed the petitioner side evidence.

Despite sufficient opportunity,
the respondent No.2 did not lead evidence, hence, respondent No.2 evidence is taken as nil.
The learned counsels for the petitioner and respondent No.2 argued on main matter and perused the records.

 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 09. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record from his mouth to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he denied to the suggestion that his uncle was riding his Motor Cycle in a zig-zag manner and caused accident and admits that he has not produced any document to show Balaji Alias Balaji V vs Manjunatha Enterprises on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69890741/

PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained raw area left foot injury and he assessed total disability of left lower limb at 40% and whole body disability at 20% and he has produced OPD book, X-ray, Original Case sheet and Relevant portion of mention of fractures sustained by the petitioner as per Ex.P.21 to 23(A).
During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that wounds are healed up and also admits that he was not the author of Ex.P.23 and 23(A) documents.
11. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24 on his behalf.

Ex.P.1 is copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending lorry for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and causing grievous (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is copy of FIR filed by the Pererasandra Police against the driver of the offending lorry for his rash and negligent driving and caused the accident.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Complaint.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is copy of IMV report which shows involvement of the offending lorry in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Letter addressed to RTO, Chikkaballapur.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Letter addressed to PSI, Pererasandra Police Station.
Ex.P.8 is copy of Bail bond.

Ex.P.11 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending vehicle.

Ex.P.12 is copy of Reply to notice,
wherein the owner has stated that he is the owner of the offending vehicle and one Naveen Kumar was driving the vehicle as on the date of accident and he had a valid driving licence and the said vehicle had valid insurance with respondent No.2 and same is valid as on the date of accident.

Ex.P.19 is Discharge summary, which discloses that the petitioner was admitted at Victoria hospital,
Bengaluru as inpatient from 16.09.2023 to 15.10.2023 nearly for 30 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.21 is OPD (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 book.
Ex.P.22 is X-ray.
Ex.P.23 is Original Case sheet.
Ex.P.23(A) is Relevant portion of Ex.P.23.
Ex.P.24 is Photographs and 24(A) is CD of Photographs.

12. On going through the oral and documentary evidence, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that the he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 16.09.2023 at about 06.30 a.m, near Kammaganahalli Village, Chikkaballapura Taluk, due to rash and negligent act of driving of Bharath Benz Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-43-A-2678 by its driver, as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 20 years and was a student studying in 5th Sem. B.Com and also doing Balaji Alias Balaji V vs Manjunatha Enterprises on 7 April, 2025

Due to accidental injuries, he has undergone pain and sufferings.

(SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 14. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.13 Voter ID card and Ex.P.20 Aadhaar card.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other evidence, the same can be relied upon, according to which, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 17.03.2003 and the alleged accident was occurred on 16.09.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is 20 years
. Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner is 20 years as on the date of accident.

15.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that he has not (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 produced any document to show his loss of academic year due to accidental injuries.

16. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, it is admitted fact that petitioner is a student as on the date of accident and he has no independent source of income and there is no evidence on record to show that petitioner has earned income.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/-
p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-
and it is multiplied by 12.
17.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained raw area left foot injury and he assessed total disability of left lower limb at 40% and whole body disability at 20%.

However,
considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 5%.
Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under;
18. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- As per Ex.P.19 Discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, as inpatient nearly for 30 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled Balaji Alias Balaji V vs Manjunatha Enterprises on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69890741/
5 for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

sentences.text: 19. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.9 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and as per Ex.P.21 OPD book.

Photographs and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

20. Loss of income during laid up period:- As already discussed above, this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,000/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 30 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 duration of his stay in hospital
, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast two months.
Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/- (Rs.16,000 x 2) under this head.
21. Medical expenses:-
As per Ex.P.15 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred total medical expenses of Rs.3,875/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,875/- under this head.

22. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
23. Future medical expenses:- The doctor PW.2 has not stated anything about future medical expenses and also not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Absolutely, there is no evidence on record to show petitioner needs another surgery or future treatment.

Therefore,
the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
24. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

sentences.text: Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,98,675/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
26. Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 Insurance Company has appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement and took several defences, but did not lead any evidence to prove its defence and to disprove the case of the petitioner.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 2 admits that it has issued insurance policy in respect of offending (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-43-A-2678 in favour of respondent No.1 and the same was valid as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.2 has not placed any material or evidence to show that owner or driver have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Tipper Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Tipper Lorry shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.2,98,675/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,98,675/- (Rupees Two lakhs ninety eight (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.7299/2023 thousand six hundred and seventy five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, the petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
